messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. The main issue is the discounted price: I won’t subsidize A’s purchase, and B and I both need a fair share. I haven’t agreed to it. I’d need us to agree openly on a fair valuation and terms before anything is decided.

I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I’m concerned we can’t move forward without C’s agreement. A good outcome would be a plan everyone can accept, though the price and shares aren’t settled.
Thank you. I’d be hoping for some money from the house to start a dance studio. I’m not sure what’s fair yet, but I’d like that possibility to be part of the discussion.
Not quite. I do want a family discount; I haven’t said affordability is the issue, or that I’m looking for a home for my family. I want a plan everyone can accept.
That wording doesn’t quite fit. A family discount would help me build financial independence. I don’t have a particular price in mind, and C hasn’t agreed.
Yes, that captures what I’m hoping for, though no price or shares are settled. I can’t speak for C or confirm her needs.
Yes, that fits. I’d add that I haven’t agreed to A buying below market; any arrangement has to protect my fair share without asking me to subsidize hers.
